Observed state: Expected package, service, agent identity, and tenant mapping are intact; one narrow dependency is proven
Evidence required: Installed package and signature; service and process state; agent and device ID; tenant and site mapping; failure-window logs; exact DNS, proxy, TLS, certificate, clock, policy, platform, or resource evidence
Preferred path: Vendor-supported repair of the verified dependency
Do not do: Do not reinstall first, disable security controls globally, or erase logs
Prerequisites: Current vendor procedure; authorized maintenance window; alternate access; rollback; expected recovery interval
Success proof: Correct identity; new heartbeat; current inventory; monitoring; fresh patch scan; bounded script; remote access where in scope; audit evidence
Stop or escalate when: The cause is unproven, repair changes identity, security evidence appears, or the endpoint is business-critical without an approved window

Observed state: Agent check-in is healthy but patching, scripting, inventory, monitoring, or remote access is stale or failing
Evidence required: Current heartbeat and identity; module status and logs; underlying platform evidence; policy and job history; last known good result
Preferred path: Repair the failed module or its underlying platform dependency
Do not do: Do not treat one module failure as proof that the whole agent must be removed
Prerequisites: Function owner; current documentation; bounded test; rollback; normal module schedule
Success proof: A new function-specific result after the normal schedule, with audit evidence and no unintended policy or identity change
Stop or escalate when: More than one module fails, the failure spans a cohort, the platform is degraded, or vendor support requires escalation

Observed state: Supported repair is unavailable or has failed; package or enrollment state is irrecoverably damaged; removal and re-enrollment behavior are documented
Evidence required: Failed repair evidence; installed identity; device and tenant mapping; official installer and removal procedure; package signature or hash; affected functions; duplicate search
Do not do: Do not use an unverified package, generic deletion commands, or uncontrolled bulk reinstall
Prerequisites: Explicit authorization; approved alternate access; correct tenant and site package; tamper-protection procedure; rollback; duplicate-record reconciliation plan
Success proof: Old agent cleanly removed; correct new identity; no duplicate automation; full functional tests; old and new records reconciled
Stop or escalate when: Removal may strand the device, identity is ambiguous, the correct package is unavailable, or rollback cannot be performed

Observed state: Device identity, tenant placement, authorization, alternate access, failure cause, or business impact is unknown
Evidence required: Current facts and gaps; preserved logs; owner; customer and site; workload criticality; last known state; unresolved identity or access evidence
Do not do: Do not restart, repair, remove, reinstall, re-enroll, or suppress alerts merely to make the dashboard green
Prerequisites: Named technical and business owner; due date; escalation route; approved next evidence-gathering step
Success proof: Missing facts resolved; authority and safe access confirmed; one evidence-based path approved
Stop or escalate when: No owner accepts the risk, suspected compromise exists, tenant boundaries are unclear, or production impact exceeds the change authority
